  • Visitors can experience live cigar rolling demonstrations, taste traditional Cuban coffee and guava pastries, and browse handmade ceramic and leather crafts from over 60 local vendors.

  • Direct Verdict: BWX Technologies is the stronger buy for risk-conscious investors due to long-term naval nuclear reactor defense contracts, while Centrus offers higher speculative growth tied to domestic HALEU enrichment capacity.

  • Both nuclear supply chain stocks tumbled in 2026 (Centrus down 54%, BWXT down 22%) after surging on AI data center clean energy demand, but both stand to benefit as the federal Prohibiting Russian Uranium Imports Act takes full effect by 2028.

📌 In-Depth Context & Background

Following the 2011 Fukushima disaster, the domestic nuclear sector experienced a decade of stagnant capital investment. However, surging electricity demand from artificial intelligence computing centers, advanced manufacturing, and national decarbonization mandates have renewed commercial demand for next-generation reactors. Both Centrus Energy and BWX Technologies occupy critical choke points in the domestic nuclear supply chain.

📊 Documented Data & Source Evidence

According to The Motley Fool's comparative equity analysis, BWX Technologies holds $1.4 billion in naval nuclear propulsion contracts with 22% gross margins and weapons-grade 93% U-235 enrichment clearances. Centrus Energy holds the sole NRC license for commercial HALEU (5% to 25% U-235) gas centrifuge enrichment, with long-term fuel commitments to Oklo and X-energy, but faces substantial near-term capital expenditure build-out costs.

🔮 Strategic Impact & Next Milestones

With the Prohibiting Russian Uranium Imports Act taking full effect in 2028, federal regulators and private utility consortiums are prioritizing domestic enrichment suppliers.
